sentences.zh: 宣和三年廢軍及縣，以遵義砦為名，隸珍州。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xuanhe the army command and county were abolished; it took the name Zunyi Stockade and came under Zhen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xuanhe (1121) the army command and county were abolished; it took the name Zunyi Stockade and came under Zhen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 思州，政和八年建，領務川、邛水、安夷三縣。

translations.literal: Si Prefecture was established in the eighth year of Zhenghe, overseeing Wuchuan, Qiongshui, and Anyi counties.
translations.idiomatic: Si Prefecture was established in the eighth year of Zhenghe (1118), overseeing Wuchuan, Qiongshui, and Anyi counties.

sentences.zh: 宣和四年，廢州為城及務川縣，以務川城為名；

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xuanhe, the prefecture was abolished and made Wuchuan City and county; it took the name Wuchuan City;
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Xuanhe (1122) the prefecture was abolished and made Wuchuan City and county; it took the name Wuchuan City;

sentences.zh: 邛水、安夷二縣皆作堡，並隸黔州。

translations.literal: Qiongshui and Anyi counties were both made forts and placed under Qian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Qiongshui and Anyi counties were both made forts and placed under Qian Prefecture.

translations.literal: In the first year of Shaoxing it was restored as Si Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shaoxing (1131) it was restored as Si Prefecture.

translations.literal: Three counties: Wuchuan, Anyi, and Qiongshui.
translations.idiomatic: It had three counties: Wuchuan, Anyi, and Qiongshui.

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xuanhe they were all abolished and placed under Qian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Xuanhe (1122) they were all abolished and placed under Qian Prefecture.

translations.literal: In the second year of Shaoxing they were restored.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Shaoxing (1132) they were restored.

translations.literal: Bozhou, seat of Leyuan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Bozhou, seat of Leyuan commandery.

sentences.zh: 大觀二年，南平夷人楊文貴等獻其地，建為州，領播川、琅川、帶水三縣。

translations.literal: In the second year of Daguan, Yang Wengui and other Yi people of Nanping submitted their lands; it was established as a prefecture overseeing Bochuan, Langchuan, and Daishui counties.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Daguan (1108) Yang Wengui and other Yi people of Nanping submitted their lands; it was established as a prefecture overseeing Bochuan, Langchuan, and Daishui counties.

sentences.zh: 宣和三年，廢為城，隸南平軍。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xuanhe it was abolished and made a city under Nanping Army Command.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xuanhe (1121) it was abolished and made a city under Nanping Army Command.

sentences.zh: 端平三年，復以白綿堡為播州，三縣仍廢，嘉熙三年，復設播州，充安撫使。

translations.literal: In the third year of Duanping, Baimian Fort was again made Bozhou; the three counties remained abolished. In the third year of Jiaxi, Bozhou was re-established and given the pacification commissioner's post.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Duanping (1236) Baimian Fort was again made Bozhou; the three counties remained abolished. In the third year of Jiaxi (1239) Bozhou was re-established and given the pacification commissioner's post.

translations.literal: At the end of the Xianchun era, Zhen Prefecture came under its jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Xianchun era, Zhen Prefecture came under its jurisdiction.

translations.literal: One county: Leyuan.
translations.idiomatic: It had one county: Leyuan.

translations.literal: Middle-grade.
translations.idiomatic: Middle-grade.

sentences.zh: 有遵義砦，開禧三年升軍，嘉定十一年復為砦。

translations.literal: It had Zunyi Stockade; in the third year of Kaixi it was promoted to an army command, and in the eleventh year of Jiading it was again made a stockade.
translations.idiomatic: It had Zunyi Stockade; in the third year of Kaixi (1207) it was elevated to an army command, and in the eleventh year of Jiading (1218) it was reduced again to a stockade.

sentences.zh: 川、峽四路，蓋《禹貢》梁、雍、荊三州之地，而梁州為多。

translations.literal: The four circuits of Chuan and Xia are broadly the lands of Liang, Yong, and Jing in the Yu Gong, with Liang predominating.
translations.idiomatic: The Four Circuits of Chuan and Xia broadly comprised the territories of Liang, Yong, and Jing described in the Yu Gong, with Liang predominating.

translations.literal: Its astral territory shares allotment with Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Its astral territory shared allotment with Qin.

sentences.zh: 南至荊峽，北控劍棧，西南接蠻夷。

translations.literal: South to Jing and the gorges, north controlling the Sword Plank Road passes, southwest reaching the Man and Yi.
translations.idiomatic: It reached south to Jing and the gorges, controlled the Sword Plank Road passes in the north, and bordered the Man and Yi in the southwest.

sentences.zh: 土植宜柘，繭絲織文纖麗者窮於天下，地狹而腴，民勤耕作，無寸土之曠，歲三四收。

translations.literal: The soil suits mulberry; silks and woven brocades finer than any under heaven; the land is narrow but fertile, the people diligent in farming, not an inch of ground left idle, and three or four harvests a year.
translations.idiomatic: The soil suited mulberry, and its cocoon silk and woven brocades were unmatched under heaven. The land was narrow but fertile; the people farmed diligently, leaving not an inch of ground idle, and gathered three or four harvests a year.

sentences.zh: 其所獲多為遨遊之費，踏青、藥市之集尤盛焉，動至連月。

translations.literal: Much of what they earned went to the cost of outings; gatherings for spring outings and medicine markets were especially grand, often lasting for months on end.
translations.idiomatic: Much of what they earned went to outings and pleasure; spring-outing and medicine-market fairs were especially lavish, often lasting for months at a time.

sentences.zh: 好音樂，少愁苦，尚奢靡，性輕揚，喜虛稱。

translations.literal: They loved music, felt little sorrow, prized luxury, were light and buoyant by nature, and delighted in empty boasts.
translations.idiomatic: They loved music, felt little sorrow, prized luxury, were by nature light and buoyant, and delighted in empty boasting.

sentences.zh: 庠塾聚學者眾，然懷土罕趨仕進。

translations.literal: Many scholars gathered in schools, yet clinging to their native soil they rarely sought advancement in office.
translations.idiomatic: Many scholars gathered in schools, yet clinging to their native places they rarely sought office and advancement.

sentences.zh: 涪陵之民尤尚鬼俗，有父母疾病，多不省視醫藥，及親在多別籍異材。

translations.literal: The people of Fuling especially honored ghost customs; when parents fell ill many did not seek doctors or medicine, and while parents still lived they set up separate registers and estates.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Fuling especially honored ghostly customs: when parents fell ill many did not call in doctors or medicine, and while parents still lived they often set up separate household registers and estates.

sentences.zh: 漢中、巴東，俗尚頗同，淪於偏方，殆將百年。

translations.literal: Hanzhong and Badong customs were much the same; lost to remote margins, nearly a hundred years.
translations.idiomatic: Hanzhong and Badong shared much the same customs; cut off in remote corners of the realm, this had lasted for nearly a century.

sentences.zh: 孟氏既平，聲教攸暨，文學之士，彬彬輩出焉。

translations.literal: After the Meng clan was pacified, culture and instruction extended there, and men of letters emerged in throngs.
translations.idiomatic: After the Meng clan was pacified, imperial culture reached them, and men of letters emerged in ever greater numbers.
